SHREYASH · you tapped pay. the signal died. why weren't you charged twice?
p2c02 · idempotency, exactly-once, and ledgers · · · · · · ·

You tapped Pay. Your signal died. The app retried.

Why weren't you charged twice?

origin · dalmellington, 2015 · horizon online, fujitsu / post office
The books balanced. The books were wrong.

A subpostmistress scanned one £8,000 pouch once. Horizon recorded it four times. The retry was honest: a script thought it had not finished and repeated its last step, and nothing remembered that the first write had happened. 112 occurrences, 88 branches, five years. People were prosecuted over ledgers that agreed with themselves.

who got hurt, and what nobody had remembered. now the mechanism.
The key travels with the request. The client minted it, once. The key is stored with the result, in the same transaction as the effect. The money moved exactly once. Now the response has to make it back. The signal died here. The client never saw the OK. The client retries with the same key. That is the whole trick. Same key: replay the response, not the work.
That's it. It's gone.
rebuild it from memory. don't scroll back; there is nothing to scroll back to.

ROHIT · a cosmic ray flips one bit, 400 km up. why doesn't the mission end?
seu · chapter 9 · · · · · · ·
A cosmic ray flips one bit in a satellite's memory, 400 km up.
Why doesn't the mission end?
1969
Apollo 11, 1202 alarm
The guidance computer overloaded, restarted itself mid-descent, and kept flying. Restart was a feature.
2003
Schaerbeek, Belgium
One flipped bit in an electronic voting machine gave a candidate 4,096 extra votes. A single bit, position 13.
2022
Voyager 1
Garbled telemetry, 23 billion km away, traced to a corrupted memory chip. Patched by moving the code around it.
hamming(12,8) · 8 bits of data carry 4 bits of proof
syndrome = p8 p4 p2 p1 = 0 1 0 1 → bit 5
seu corrected · 1
flight counter0x2A
program counter0x0800_1F3C 2 bits flipped · uncorrectable
watchdog1.6 s
eccon
RESET
state restored from checkpoint · counter 0x2A · mission continues
The extra bits let the reader compute which bit lied. One flip: caught and fixed. Two flips: caught, not fixed.

ANANYA · you step off a curb. your knee catches you before you decide to.
chapter 11 · impedance control · a spring you can argue with · · · · · · ·
You step off a curb. Your knee catches you before you decide to.
How does a powered exoskeleton do that in ten milliseconds without throwing you?
she knows this shape. it is a state machine with a 1 kHz tick, not a 60 Hz frame. every transition is a guard on the trace.
τ = K (θd − θ) − B θ̇
K · how hard the joint argues back
B · how fast it stops arguing
at heel strike: θd holds, K rises. the joint becomes a spring you can lean on.
K = 40 · B = 0.5
sense → decide → act: 1 ms. human reflex: 30–50 ms. the exo gets there first, so it must never be wrong.
That's it. It's gone.
write the torque law. say what B does.
